scenes.dialogue: Your cheque has bounced. So when must you send notice, how long does the drawer get to pay, and when can you file a complaint?
scenes.chip: 1 · FOUR CLOCKS AFTER A BOUNCED CHEQUE

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. A complaint under Section One Thirty Eight of the Negotiable Instruments Act runs on four separate legal clocks.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. A complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act runs on four separate legal clocks.

scenes.dialogue: First, the essentials. The bounced cheque must relate to a legally enforceable debt or liability, and the statutory conditions must be met.
In Rangappa versus Sri Mohan, the Supreme Court confirmed a rebuttable presumption for the holder, once the necessary foundation is established.
That foundation includes the drawer's signature. The drawer can still raise a probable defence.
A security cheque may also attract liability, when the secured debt has become payable and remains unpaid.
Clock one starts with the cheque's date. The Act itself mentions six months, or the cheque's validity, whichever is earlier.
R B I directions limit ordinary cheque validity to three months. Do not assume ninety days. A postdated cheque becomes payable on its stated date.
scenes.shown: RBI directions limit ordinary cheque validity to three months. Do not assume 90 days. A postdated cheque becomes payable on its stated date.

scenes.dialogue: Deposit early enough to reach the drawee bank in time. Ishar Alloy explains why a last minute deposit at your collecting bank may be insufficient.
scenes.shown: Deposit early enough to reach the drawee bank in time. Ishar Alloy explains why a last-minute deposit at your collecting bank may be insufficient.

scenes.dialogue: Clock two begins when the payee receives the bank's information that the cheque was returned unpaid. Within thirty days, give the drawer a written demand notice.
scenes.shown: Clock two begins when the payee receives the bank's information that the cheque was returned unpaid. Within 30 days, give the drawer a written demand notice.

scenes.dialogue: Record both the memo date, and when the information actually reached you. Clearly identify the cheque, and demand its amount.
If interest or costs are claimed, state them separately. Suman Sethi explains why the cheque amount must be identifiable.
Dispatch and receipt dates serve different purposes. The payment clock turns on receipt, including legally presumed service where applicable.
C C Alavi Haji explains the rebuttable presumption for a correctly addressed notice sent by registered post.
scenes.shown: C.C. Alavi Haji explains the rebuttable presumption for a correctly addressed notice sent by registered post.

scenes.dialogue: Refusal or avoidance does not necessarily defeat service. Keep the signed notice, postal records and address proof, and never invent a delivery date.
Clock three gives the drawer fifteen days after receipt of the notice to pay the cheque amount. Exclude the receipt date when counting.
scenes.shown: Clock three gives the drawer 15 days after receipt of the notice to pay the cheque amount. Exclude the receipt date when counting.

scenes.dialogue: Payment within this period prevents the cause of action from arising on that notice. A reply denying liability is not payment, and it does not stop the clock.
There is no separate statutory reply deadline. A drawer who disputes the demand should still reply promptly, with records.
If unpaid after those fifteen days, the cause of action arises on the next day. Do not file early, even if the drawer has rejected the demand.
scenes.shown: If unpaid after those 15 days, the cause of action arises on the next day. Do not file early, even if the drawer has rejected the demand.

scenes.dialogue: In Yogendra Pratap Singh versus Savitri Pandey, the Supreme Court held that filing before the payment period expires is not maintainable.
Later cognizance cannot cure a premature complaint; a fresh one may need delay condoned.
Clock four is one calendar month from the cause of action, not a fixed thirty days. Econ Antri confirms that the cause of action date is excluded.
scenes.shown: Clock four is one calendar month from the cause of action, not a fixed 30 days. Econ Antri confirms that the cause of action date is excluded.
scenes.chip: 6 · CLOCK FOUR: FILE WITHIN ONE MONTH

scenes.dialogue: A delayed complaint may be entertained if the court accepts sufficient cause under the proviso to Section One Forty Two.
scenes.shown: A delayed complaint may be entertained if the court accepts sufficient cause under the proviso to Section 142.

scenes.dialogue: But a delayed notice is different; this proviso does not excuse it. Negotiations and promises to pay do not, by themselves, extend the filing deadline.
Here is a fictional example. The cheque was presented within validity, and the bank's dishonour information reached the payee on first May.
scenes.shown: Here is a fictional example. The cheque was presented within validity, and the bank's dishonour information reached the payee on 1 May.

scenes.dialogue: Notice was dispatched on second May, and actually received on sixth May. So the payment days run from seventh to twenty first May.
scenes.shown: Notice was dispatched on 2 May, and actually received on 6 May. So the payment days run from 7 to 21 May.

scenes.dialogue: If unpaid, the cause of action arises on twenty second May, and the ordinary complaint window runs to twenty second June.
scenes.shown: If unpaid, the cause of action arises on 22 May, and the ordinary complaint window runs to 22 June.

scenes.dialogue: These dates assume proven actual receipt, no intervening payment, and no special court closure or extension issue.
Now file a written complaint. It must be made by the payee or holder in due course, before the competent Magistrate.
For collection through an account, jurisdiction ordinarily follows the payee's account branch, even if deposited at another branch of that bank.
Presentation otherwise than through an account follows the drawer's bank branch. Also check the special rule for subsequent complaints against the same drawer.
Organise the cheque, return memo, debt records, notice, service proof and date calculation, together with the required synopsis and affidavits.
Avoid treating every return memo as automatic guilt, confusing a reply with payment, or filing early.
A cheque may be presented again within its validity. M S R Leathers permits prosecution on a subsequent dishonour, if all conditions are met.
scenes.shown: A cheque may be presented again within its validity. MSR Leathers permits prosecution on a subsequent dishonour, if all conditions are met.

scenes.dialogue: But a reminder notice alone, without a fresh dishonour, does not restart the clock.
After the payment window, document any later payment. It does not automatically erase the case; settlement or compounding needs legal steps.
Remember the sequence. Present within the cheque's validity, ordinarily three months. Send notice within thirty days of receiving the bank's information.
scenes.shown: Remember the sequence. Present within the cheque's validity, ordinarily three months. Send notice within 30 days of receiving the bank's information.

scenes.dialogue: Allow fifteen days after notice receipt for payment. Then file within one calendar month of the cause of action. And keep proof for every date.
scenes.shown: Allow 15 days after notice receipt for payment. Then file within one calendar month of the cause of action. And keep proof for every date.

scenes.dialogue: Those four clocks, supported by the underlying debt and proper service, form the foundation of a cheque dishonour complaint.
